newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Greek troops land in distressed Albania.
newsitem.headline: Greek troops land in distressed Albania.

text.p: The first Greek troops in a multi-national force safeguarding humanitarian aid in chaotic Albania arrived at Tirana airport on Wednesday and headed for the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, officials said.

"One hundred and twenty soldiers, mainly infantry, are coming today. Two military aircraft have landed so far. Another four planes are expected later," Dimitris Moustaklis, a spokesman at the Greek embassy, told Reuters.
In Athens, defence ministry sources said the soldiers were flown in C-130 planes from the northern city of Salonika to Tirana and the navy ship Samos sailed with another 130 troops.
The Samos, which is also carrying tanks, is expected to reach Vlore on Friday.
Greece, concerned with the crisis on its northern border, has pledged about 700 men to the Italian-led eight-nation force of 6,000 soldiers.
The rest of the Greek troops will leave for Albania in the next few days, defence sources in Athens said.
Some 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish soldiers from the U.N.-approved force began arriving in Albania by air and sea on Tuesday.
Its mission is to protect the distribution of much-need aid to the small Balkan state, which has been rocked by violence since the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes earlier this year.
Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured in several weeks of armed anarchy and banditry in Europe's poorest nation.
